articles.title: Tom Aspinall: Is It the Eye or the Contract?
articles.description: Daniel Cormier wants the UFC to get Tom Aspinall back into the Octagon as soon as possible. Chael Sonnen agrees but there’s one question nobody seems willing to answer. Is Tom Aspinall healthy? Chael examines the possibilities behind Aspinall’s continued absence. Maybe the UFC already has his next fight in place and simply hasn’t announced it. Maybe there’s a contract issue behind the scenes. Or perhaps the eye injury Aspinall suffered against Ciryl Gane still hasn’t healed enough for him to return. And if it is the eye, Chael says Aspinall deserves some grace. Chael also revisits his own immediate reaction to the Gane fight and explains why learning the severity of Tom’s injury changed his perspective. Whenever Aspinall does return, Chael believes the path leads directly back to Ciryl Gane. But before discussing opponents, contracts or championship fights, there’s a much simpler question that needs answering: Is Tom Aspinall healthy enough to fight? #ChaelSonnen #TomAspinall #CirylGane #DanielCormier #UFC #MMABad Guy Inc merch now available at https://BadGuyInc.com Click here to subscribe: https://bit.ly/3FrHIPK Follow me on IG: https://bit.ly/3HY7BIE Follow me on Twitter: https://bit.ly/3tvY5J7 Follow me on Threads https://www.threads.com/@sonnench

articles.title: Usman Nurmagomedov Turned Down $2 MILLION
articles.description: Usman Nurmagomedov reportedly turned down a $2 million offer from the PFL and Chael Sonnen believes he may be taking a serious risk. Usman is entering free agency after completing his PFL deal, but there’s an important detail: turning down $2 million doesn’t mean there’s a bigger UFC offer waiting for him. Right now, Chael argues, there may be no competing offer at all. So why walk away? Chael breaks down the difference between having a massive number written into a contract and actually having enough fights to collect it. A smaller deal with consistent activity can ultimately be worth far more than a huge purse attached to a fighter who rarely gets booked. But Usman Nurmagomedov presents another possibility. For fighters from the Dagestani camp, money may not be the only motivation. Usman already has financial security. What he may want now is competition, exposure and the opportunity to build his legacy on the biggest possible stage. Did Usman make a mistake turning down $2 million — or is he betting on something bigger than money? articles.title: The Truth About UFC’s “Rich Kid” Arman Tsarukyan
articles.description: Paddy Pimblett dismissed Arman Tsarukyan as nothing more than the son of a rich father. Chael Sonnen sees it completely differently. Paddy has become one of the UFC’s biggest stars without changing the personality that made people care about him in the first place. He’s still outspoken, confrontational and willing to create rivalries. But when it comes to Arman Tsarukyan, Chael believes Paddy may be missing what makes Arman’s story so impressive. Arman didn’t need fighting to change his financial situation. He didn’t need MMA for fame or money. Yet he still chose the wrestling rooms, the MMA gyms, the brutal training camps and the sacrifices required to compete at the highest level. Chael explains why coming from money doesn’t diminish Arman’s accomplishments it may actually make them more interesting. Tsarukyan continues to compete constantly, train alongside everyone else and pursue the toughest challenges available without needing the sport financially. So does being a “rich man’s son” hurt Arman Tsarukyan’s story? Chael argues it does the exact opposite. articles.title: I am NOT taunting the West Linn Police
articles.description: Chael Sonnen has found himself in a situation with the West Linn Police Department and he'd like to make one thing very clear: he's not taunting anybody. When Chael works live for Paramount, he has to be in his studio chair at a very specific time. The problem? Parking around the office has become nearly impossible, and even though Chael pays for his own spot, someone else occasionally parks there without realizing it's reserved. So when the clock is ticking, Chael has resorted to parking his truck in a yellow zone. The result is predictable: a $30 ticket. Chael isn't complaining. He knows he's parked illegally, considers the ticket a cost of doing business and pays it every time. But after doing this repeatedly, he's developed a new concern: what if the officer writing these tickets thinks Chael is intentionally ignoring him? That's when a $30 parking problem could become something considerably more complicated. Consider this Chael's public message to the West Linn Police: he respects the rules, he respects the ticket, and he promises he's not trying to start a feud. Now he needs to go move his truck. #ChaelSonnen #WestLinn #Oregon #BadGuyIncBad Guy Inc merch now available at https://BadGuyInc.com Click here to subscribe: https://bit.ly/3FrHIPK Follow me on IG: https://bit.ly/3HY7BIE Follow me on Twitter: https://bit.ly/3tvY5J7 Follow me on Threads https://www.threads.com/@sonnench

articles.title: The Truth About Dillon Danis Pulling Out
articles.description: Dillon Danis was accused of no-showing his fight with Mike Perry. Chael Sonnen has one problem with that story: Danis reportedly called to tell the promotion he wasn’t coming. That’s not a no-show. Chael initially had the same reaction as everyone else. Walking away from a fight after tickets are sold, an opponent is booked and the media tour is complete would be a terrible move. But then more information came out. Danis was reportedly dealing with an injury that required hospital treatment, and he contacted the promotion before the event to let them know he couldn’t compete. That changes the story. Chael explains the major difference between abandoning an event without warning and suffering a last-minute injury that prevents a fighter from being medically cleared. Fighters have been forced out at the last minute before, and that isn’t the same thing as simply refusing to show up. You can criticize Dillon Danis for plenty of things. But Chael argues you can’t call something a “no-show” while simultaneously acknowledging that he called to tell you he wasn’t coming. #ChaelSonnen #DillonDanis #MikePerry #MMA #CombatSportsBad Guy Inc merch now available at https://BadGuyInc.com Click here to subscribe: https://bit.ly/3FrHIPK Follow me on IG: https://bit.ly/3HY7BIE Follow me on Twitter: https://bit.ly/3tvY5J7 Follow me on Threads https://www.threads.com/@sonnench

articles.title: What If Arman Loses?
articles.description: Mauricio Ruffy is a sizable underdog against Arman Tsarukyan, but Chael Sonnen wants one question answered before they ever step into the Octagon: if Ruffy wins, does he get Justin Gaethje? Chael was told this five-round co-main event was being treated as a true No. 1 contender fight. If that's the case, the stakes can't only apply to Tsarukyan. MMA has a history of calling fights “No. 1 contender” bouts when what it really means is one specific fighter gets a title shot if he wins. If the underdog pulls off the upset, suddenly the conversation changes. Chael doesn't want that happening here. He also shares what Ruffy and Tsarukyan told him personally about preparing for five rounds. Ruffy was measured and confident. Arman had a very different response: 25 minutes simply gives him more time to “teach this young guy a lesson.” Before debating who wins, Chael wants the UFC and the MMA community to preserve what makes this matchup important. If Ruffy beats Tsarukyan, he shouldn't have to make another argument. articles.title: I want to Believe Tyson Fury
articles.description: Tyson Fury says he didn't really train for Francis Ngannou because, in his mind, it wasn't a real fight. Chael Sonnen has a problem with that explanation. Chael isn't accusing Fury of lying. But he doesn't like revisionist history, and what happened inside the ring makes Fury's version difficult to understand. Fury looked prepared. More importantly, when the fight became unexpectedly competitive, he was able to dig deep and win the later rounds. Chael explains why that kind of conditioning and resilience usually comes from doing the work beforehand. And none of this should take away from Francis Ngannou. Chael still considers Ngannou's performance against Fury one of the most remarkable accomplishments he's ever witnessed in sports. A fighter with no professional boxing experience came within one judge's scorecard of defeating the heavyweight champion of the world. If Fury truly didn't train, Chael will accept it. But if this is an attempt to rewrite what happened that night, he has one request for Tyson: tell the story the way it actually happened. #TysonFury #FrancisNgannou #Boxing #ChaelSonnen #MMA Bad Guy Inc merch now available at https://BadGuyInc.com Click here to subscribe: https://bit.ly/3FrHIPK Follow me on IG: https://bit.ly/3HY7BIE Follow me on Twitter: https://bit.ly/3tvY5J7 Follow me on Threads https://www.threads.com/@sonnench

articles.title: Is Tom Aspinall About to Lose His UFC Title? #ufc
articles.description: Is Tom Aspinall about to lose his UFC heavyweight championship? Chael Sonnen isn't saying it has happened — but he's seeing signs that something is moving behind the scenes. Chael points to Curtis Blaydes? No. The heavyweight picture is centered around Tom Aspinall and Ciryl Gane, and Chael believes the moves being made by other contenders could indicate that people inside the UFC have information about Tom's timeline that the public doesn't. Dana White previously made it clear that Gane would get another opportunity against Aspinall after their first fight. Gane then put his position at the top of the division on the line against Alex Pereira. Now, however, another possibility appears to be emerging. Gane vs. Jailton Almeida? Chael questions why the heavyweight division isn't focused on the rematch everyone expected — and why the conversation instead seems to be shifting toward Gane fighting another contender. If Tom can't return in time, does the UFC strip the champion? Could Ciryl Gane become the undisputed UFC heavyweight champion without beating Aspinall? Chael explains why the current heavyweight situation has him paying very close attention. #TomAspinall #CirylGane #UFC #UFCHeavyweight #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #AlexPereira #MMAAnalysis #UFCChampionship

articles.title: Tom Aspinall Says He's NOT Leaving the UFC
articles.description: Tom Aspinall says he isn't leaving the UFC. That's good news but Chael Sonnen still has one question: when is Tom actually coming back? After months of uncertainty surrounding Aspinall's injury, recovery and future at heavyweight, Chael has struggled to find any reliable information suggesting the UFC heavyweight champion is back in the gym and preparing to compete. Even people close to Aspinall's circle aren't hearing that he's firing on all cylinders. Tom's latest statement eliminates one possibility: he isn't planning to leave the UFC. But Chael argues that “I'm not leaving” isn't quite the same thing as “I'm ready to fight.” Meanwhile, Ciryl Gane holds the interim heavyweight championship, and eventually the division has to move forward. If Gane fights again before Aspinall can return, Chael believes it should be for the undisputed heavyweight championship rather than another interim title defense. articles.title: Charles Oliveira’s Argument Is Hard to Ignore #ufc
articles.description: Charles Oliveira has one argument that is very difficult to get around: “I beat your champion.” Chael Sonnen breaks down Charles' case for fighting Islam Makhachev next — and why it's not nearly as simple as it sounds. Oliveira is the reigning BMF champion, and there's precedent for the BMF title serving as a pathway to an undisputed championship opportunity. Max Holloway used that accomplishment to earn a shot at the lightweight title. But Chael isn't convinced Charles should automatically get the next opportunity. There's still the Arman Tsarukyan situation. There's also the question of Michael Morales and the other contenders making their case. If another top contender steps up, beats Arman, and puts together the kind of performance Chael expects, the UFC could have a compelling reason to go in another direction. Then there's the history between Charles and Arman. Charles was previously scheduled to fight Tsarukyan but withdrew — and Chael questions whether a fighter should be rewarded with a championship opportunity after pulling out of another matchup. Still, Charles' argument remains powerful. He beat the champion. So does that make Charles Oliveira the rightful next challenger for Islam Makhachev? #CharlesOliveira #IslamMakhachev #ArmanTsarukyan #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #BMF #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #LightweightMMA

articles.title: Islam Has Three Names Left on His Hit List #ufc
articles.description: Islam Makhachev has revealed his own hit list — and Chael Sonnen thinks it's one of the coolest things a champion can say. According to Islam, there are three names left that he wants to handle before he's finished with the sport: Carlos Prates, Michael Morales, and Shavkat Rakhmonov. Chael agrees that those are the three guys. But completing that list won't happen quickly. Three fights could take roughly a year and a half, especially when injuries, scheduling, and the realities of MMA are factored in. And there are still plenty of unanswered questions. Can Islam beat Prates? Can he beat Morales? Can he beat Rakhmonov? We don't know — and that's exactly why the fights have to happen. Chael also discusses Rakhmonov's injury and why time away from competition doesn't make an athlete better. If you're not training and competing, you're not developing your skills. When Rakhmonov eventually returns, he'll have to prove he's still the same fighter. But the bigger story is Islam's mindset. He's essentially telling the world: I'm not leaving until I handle this business. Three elite contenders. Three massive challenges. And a champion who apparently wants to settle all of it himself. #IslamMakhachev #CarlosPrates #MichaelMorales #ShavkatRakhmonov #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #UFCChampionship

articles.title: Name 15 UFC Heavyweights Better Than Gable
articles.description: Why isn't Gable Steveson ranked in the UFC heavyweight division? Chael Sonnen doesn't buy the explanation. The rankings committee says a fighter generally has to beat someone already inside the top 15 before earning a spot. But Chael points out that once fighters are ranked, the committee moves them up and down constantly even when they haven't competed. So why is breaking into the rankings treated differently? Chael challenges anyone to name 15 UFC heavyweights they genuinely believe would beat Gable Steveson. He also brings Jon Jones into the discussion: Dana White has repeatedly said that if Jones returns, he'll fight for a title, despite Jones currently being unranked. If an unranked fighter can immediately fight for a championship, what exactly are the rankings supposed to represent? Chael argues that rankings matter for matchmaking, contracts, sponsorships and fighter careers so if the UFC is going to publish them, the committee should rank who they actually believe are the best fighters.
